(Chicago, Illinois) | college = * [[Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball|Illinois State]] (2019–2022) * [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2022–2024) | highlights = * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]], [[The Sporting News|SN]] ([[2024 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2024]]) * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2024) * SEC co-Sixth Man of the Year (2023) * Second-team All-[[Missouri Valley Conference|MVC]] (2022) }} '''Antonio Reeves''' (born November 20, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball|Illinois State Redbirds]] and the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==High school career== After a prep career at [[Shadow Mountain High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]] and [[Simeon Career Academy]] in his hometown [[Chicago]], Reeves committed to [[Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball|Illinois State]] over offers from several other [[mid-major]] programs. ==College career== ===Illinois State=== Reeves was a key contributor for his first two seasons, earning a spot on the [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC) all-bench team as a sophomore. He declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], but ultimately chose to return to the Redbirds for his junior season. In the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]], Reeves averaged a career high 20.1 points per game And was named second-team All-MVC, however the team was not successful and coach [[Dan Muller (basketball)|Dan Muller]] was fired. With the coaching change, Reeves decided to transfer to a winning program.{{cite web | last = Bourne | first = Isaac | url = https://www.midmajormadness.com/2023/12/22/24008018/antonio-reeves-from-mid-major-star-to-kentucky-standout | title = Antonio Reeves: From mid-major star to Kentucky Wildcat standout | date = December 22, 2023| website = midmajormadness.com| publisher = [[SB Nation]] | access-date = January 18, 2024| quote = }} ===Kentucky=== Reeves ultimately chose Kentucky and coach [[John Calipari]]. {{cite web | last1 = Borzello | first1 = Jeff | last2 = Biancardi | first2 = Paul | url = https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33815244/antonio-reeves-transfers-illinois-state-play-basketball-kentucky-wildcats | title = Antonio Reeves transfers from Illinois State to play basketball for Kentucky Wildcats | date = April 27, 2022| website = espn.com| publisher = [[ESPN]] | access-date = January 18, 2024| quote = }}{{cite web | last = Hale | first = Jon | url = https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2022/04/27/antonio-reeves-kentucky-basketball-transfer-brings-scoring-ability/7354419001/ | title = What to know about Kentucky basketball's newest incoming transfer Antonio Reeves | date = April 27, 2022| website = courier-journal.com| publisher = [[Courier Journal]] | access-date = January 18, 2024| quote = }} As a senior, he mostly came off the bench for the Wildcats and ranked second on the team in scoring behind [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] [[Oscar Tshiebwe]] at 14.4 points per game. At the close of the season, Reeves was named the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) co-Sixth Man of the Year. {{cite web | url = https://ukathletics.com/news/2023/03/06/antonio-reeves-named-co-sixth-man-of-the-year-to-lead-wildcat-league-honorees/ | title = Antonio Reeves Named Co-Sixth Man of the Year to Lead Wildcat League Honorees | date = March 6, 2023| website = ukathletics.com| publisher = [[Kentucky Wildcats]] | access-date = January 18, 2024| quote = }} He again tested the NBA draft waters and considered another transfer, but ultimately chose to return to Kentucky for a fifth year granted to players whose eligibility was affected by the [[COVID-19]] pandemic.{{cite web | last = Salerno | first = Cameron | url = https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/antonio-reeves-returns-to-kentucky-senior-guard-expected-to-rejoin-team-after-rollercoaster-offseason/ | title = Kentucky: Senior guard expected to rejoin team after rollercoaster offseason | date = June 21, 2023| website = cbssports.com| publisher = [[CBS Sports]] | access-date = January 18, 2024| quote = }} Entering his fifth year, Reeves was named preseason second-team All-SEC.{{cite web | last = Fisher | first = Chris | url = https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/antonio-reeves-justin-edwards-kentucky-basketball-coaches-preseason-all-sec-219381691/ | title = Pair of Wildcats named Coaches Preseason All-SEC | date = November 2, 2023| website = 247sports.com| publisher = [[247Sports]] | access-date = January 18, 2024| quote = }} As the season wore in, Reeves emerged as a key player for the Wildcats and senior presence for their talented recruiting class. In January 2024, he was named to the 25-man [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden Award]] midseason watch list in recognition of his performance, along with teammate [[Reed Sheppard]].{{cite web | last = Barry | first = Armando | url =
